title: Recoveries Unit Basis for the Amount Recovered on a Travel Protection Policy
content:
What the insurer recovers against a settled claim on the Travel Protection Plans is the lower of the
settlement the compensation answers and the compensation available to the insurer, and never less than nothing.

## The quantities entering the figure

| Quantity | What it is, and from which record |
|---|---|
| The settlement the compensation answers | The payment standing last on the policy's claim record |
| The window counted | 12 months, ending on the day the recovery is booked |
| The compensation counted | The money the carrier has paid out on the traveller's bookings in the twelve months before the day the recovery is booked, together with the travel credit counted |
| The travel credit counted | Nothing |
| What is set aside for the traveller | Nothing |
| The compensation available to the insurer | The compensation counted less what is set aside for the traveller |

The recovery is rounded to two decimal places once, at the end, and no intermediate figure is rounded.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

A policy's claim record shows, as its last payment, a settlement of 840.00. The carrier's ledger for the
traveller's bookings shows 1200.00 paid out in the twelve months to the day the recovery is booked. The travel
credit counted is nothing, so the compensation counted is 1200.00; nothing is set aside for the traveller, so
the compensation available to the insurer is 1200.00 as well. The lower of 840.00 and 1200.00 is 840.00, and the
recovery is 840.00.

Take the same policy with 512.35 paid out by the carrier in those twelve months instead. The compensation
available is then 512.35, which is lower than the settlement of 840.00, and the recovery is 512.35. Take it once
more with nothing paid out by the carrier at all: the compensation available is nothing, the lower of the two
quantities is nothing, and the recovery is 0.00, a recovery being never less than nothing. The figures in these
three readings are hypothetical.
